prompt: According to this module, which of the following is NOT one of the three specific reasons AI/ML concepts are hard to explain to true beginners?
choices: AI/ML vocabulary borrows words from human cognition ("thinks", "understands", "hallucinated") that import the wrong intuitions
The actual unit of computation (tokens, vectors, attention weights) is invisible in the product's chat interface
Beginners arrive with strong wrong priors from science fiction and hype that have to be actively displaced
AI/ML concepts fundamentally require calculus that a true beginner hasn't learned yet

prompt: Why does the module recommend opening a "What is a token?" tutorial with the real, well-documented letter-counting failure (e.g. miscounting the r's in "strawberry") rather than a diagram of a tokenizer?
choices: It's a real, verifiable, surprising failure that only makes sense once the reader learns the model operates on subword tokens rather than letters or words
It proves that language models can never be trained to count correctly under any architecture
It's an unverified rumor, so the module recommends citing it without any way for the reader to check it
Token boundaries are identical across every tokenizer vocabulary, so the example generalizes perfectly to any model

prompt: The module recommends a live in-browser tokenizer visualizer (like tiktokenizer.vercel.app) as the primary tool for the beginner tutorial's hook. What's the main reason it's preferred over a Python snippet for this specific audience?
choices: It trains a brand-new custom tokenizer live for whatever text the reader pastes in
The target reader can't run Python, so a no-install browser tool lets them verify the claim themselves instead of just trusting the author
It is the only tool that can correctly tokenize English text
It removes the need for the tutorial to ever mention byte-pair encoding

prompt: In the worked feedback example, a beginner reader asked whether a "vector" was different from the token's "ID number" that the tutorial had already mentioned. What did this question reveal about the original explanation?
choices: The reader clearly had not read the earlier part of the tutorial at all
The explanation collapsed two distinct mechanistic steps (ID lookup, then embedding-matrix row lookup) into one sentence with no marked transition, inviting the reader to conflate them
The explanation was too mathematically rigorous for the intended audience
A vector and a token ID are in fact the same object, so the confusion reflected the true mechanism

prompt: The module's fix for the token-ID-vs-vector confusion explicitly ties back to a specific line of code the learner already traced in an earlier tier. Which one?
choices: nanoGPT's self.transformer.wte(idx) embedding lookup in model.py, traced during Tier 3's "Reading Real Code" module
configurator.py's exec() trick for overwriting train.py's global namespace
The LLM-as-judge faithfulness rubric from Tier 4's evaluation module
The Reflexion self-reflection loop from Tier 4's agentic systems module

prompt: In the pairing-session guidance, why does the module recommend swapping driver/navigator roles strictly on a visible timer, even in the middle of a task, rather than waiting for a natural stopping point?
choices: Interpretability experiments never have natural stopping points, so timers are the only option
Swapping mid-task forces the incoming navigator to actively reconstruct and track the current state, instead of having only half-watched
It's required by a formal pair-programming certification standard referenced in the module
It guarantees the driver never introduces a bug during their turn

prompt: A study-group facilitator asks "any questions?" after a paper walkthrough and gets silence. What concrete fix does the module recommend instead?
choices: End the session early, since silence indicates everyone understood the material
Replace the open prompt with a structured task, e.g. "everyone write down one thing you'd bet money is wrong, then we go around"
Have the presenter repeat the exact same explanation, louder and slower
Permanently move the group to an asynchronous-only, no-meeting format

prompt: The module notes that a common wrong prior beginners bring to a "how does RAG work" explanation is confusing retrieval with which other process?
choices: Byte-pair encoding tokenization
Fine-tuning — the belief that the model's weights are being retrained on the retrieved documents
Gradient descent during pretraining
The causal attention mask
